Hi Amy / Tom,

Thanks again for carving out time today — great discussion and helpful context on the platform use cases. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

1) Stakeholder roster — can you confirm the contacts below so we loop the right owners?
   - Economic buyer / procurement sponsor: Priya Rao (VP Product) — we have an intro but can you confirm email?
   - Security reviewer: Tom Hsu (you) — noted.
   - Legal / procurement contact: (we'll need a contract point-of-contact to line up T&Cs).

2) Security kickoff & scope intake — attached is our lightweight questionnaire (security_questionnaire_v1.xlsx) and an example scope diagram. Please fill what you can; Tom, if there's anything you want us to pre-populate, tell us and we will. Key items to clarify: systems in scope (production vs. non-prod), data residency, expected traffic patterns, and log/retention needs.

3) Timeline & procurement hand-off
   - If we can get the roster + questionnaire back by EOD Friday (11/27), we can schedule a 30–45m technical kickoff the following week.
   - Lauren (cc) will own pricing/PO path and Ben will assist on contract mechanics.

4) Action items for us: attach the questionnaire and a blank scope diagram; I will also send our SOC2 summary and sample DPA after this thread.

Attachments: [security_questionnaire_v1.xlsx (xlsx)], [initial_scope_diagram.png (image)]

Thanks — appreciate it.

Thanks Nikhil — good recap. Confirming roster and a few notes: 

- Priya Rao (VP Product) — priya.rao@atlasbank.com — she will act as the executive sponsor for budget and product fit.
- Legal / procurement: copying in our procurement manager (will drop the exact email tomorrow) — procurement will want the SOW, sample contract, and estimated MTCS.
- Security reviewer: Tom Hsu (copied) will lead the technical review and run the questionnaire.

Tom, we expect the primary systems in scope to be: customer-facing API endpoints (prod cluster), a small set of internal ETL jobs that pull sanitized PII for enrichment (non-prod), and S3-backed model artifact storage. Data residency: all production data must remain in our US region (us-east-1).

We should be able to return the questionnaire by EOD Thursday (11/26) — Tom, does that work?

Amy Zhao
Head of Platform Partnerships, Atlas Bank

From: Tom Hsu <thsu@atlasbank.com>

Subject: Re: Next steps: stakeholder roster, procurement hand-off & security scope kickoff

On Mon, Nov 23, 2026 at 04:03 PM Amy Zhao <amy@atlasbank.com> wrote:
> Tom, we expect the primary systems in scope to be: customer-facing API endpoints (prod cluster), a small set of internal ETL jobs that pull sanitized PII for enrichment (non-prod), and S3-backed model artifact storage.
> Data residency: all production data must remain in our US region (us-east-1).

Thanks Amy — that matches my initial read. A few clarifications and asks from security before the kickoff: 

- Scope boundary: we need to explicitly list which Redwood-hosted endpoints will accept customer data (API gateway endpoints) vs. which flows are purely internal (batch ETL).
- Minimal evidence set for kickoff: SOC 2 summary, network diagram (we'll need to map firewall rules / VPC peering), encryption-at-rest details for S3, and KMS integration notes.
- Logging / retention: we prefer 90-day app logs, 365-day audit logs. Will need to confirm Redwood's retention capabilities and cost impact.
- Data processing: confirm whether Redwood will process raw PII in any pipeline stage or only tokenized/sanitized data.

I'll start populating the questionnaire and will attach a short note inline where I need more detail. Expect our completed draft by EOD Thursday.

Tom Hsu
Security Engineer, Atlas Bank
thsu@atlasbank.com

  • Flag the scope items you called out in the kickoff agenda.
- Lauren — can you prepare an initial pricing sketch for a 6–12 month pilot with the following guardrails? Production API (burst to 50rps), non-prod ETL access for enrichment (limited dataset), and S3 model storage. We need a simple estimate we can share with Priya ahead of the legal loop.
- Ben — I will ask you to lead the procurement introduction once we have the final PO contact.

Proposed next meeting: 30 min technical kickoff with Tom + security, Lauren, Ben and myself on Tue 12/01 at 10:00am PT — does that slot look OK? If so I'll send an invite and include a short agenda covering scope boundaries, evidence list, and timeline to completion.
